clue.text: Herb finally cured problem

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word cured

parts.note: an ill is a trouble or problem

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy at last cleared up someone's ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery culinary plant, a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: Gordon MacDonald, for two bucks, meets a Yankee

parts.note: bucks are male animals, and rams are male sheep, so two of them are RAMS
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone called Gordon MacDonald hunts deer and meets an American.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sandwich: the answer completes both Gordon Ramsay, the TV chef, and Ramsay MacDonald, the first Labour Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of celebrity chef Gordon and the forename of Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald are the same word.

clue.text: Stoma (hole after surgery) is disgusting

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges, so the letters of the words before it are reordered

explanation.surface: A patient finds the stoma left by an operation repulsive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after surgery' is the anagram signal, not a medical aside: the bracket makes it look like a gloss on 'Stoma'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome describes something that causes hatred or revulsion, the same as being repellent.

clue.text: Groups following proceedings

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
legal actions are court proceedings

explanation.surface: Bands of people tracking a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Factions are small dissenting parties or cliques within a larger body.

clue.text: Barrier on waterway under pressure provides protection from water

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
in a down answer, the waterway sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water
P is the physics symbol for pressure
a course, as in watercourse, is a channel of running water

explanation.surface: A dam on a pressurised river keeps flooding at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: A damp course is a waterproof layer laid in a wall to stop moisture rising from the ground, a standard British building term.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp-proof course is a barrier in brickwork that keeps rising damp out of a building.

clue.text: City in a whirl

parts.note: to be in is to be fashionable, which is chic
to give something a whirl is to have a go at it

explanation.surface: A town that is in a spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a whirl' reads as one phrase, but splits into three pieces: in (fashionable), a, and whirl (an attempt).
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large city in Illinois, USA.

clue.text: Man supported by the Spanish church

indicators.note: in a down clue, the man sits on top of the next piece

parts.note: a chap is a man
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A fellow is backed by the Spanish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, or a nonconformist church.

clue.text: Perhaps wax can be obtained from marine mammal, one in a colony

parts.note: a seal is a sea-dwelling mammal
ants live in colonies, so one of them is an ant

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether wax can be harvested from a seal or an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax is one example of a substance used to seal joints and surfaces against air or water.

clue.text: Sound of wave motion

indicators.note: the following word is to be heard rather than read, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: a sine wave is the basic smooth oscillation, so wave suggests sine

explanation.surface: The noise of waves moving.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a gesture, a movement of the hand that conveys meaning.

clue.text: Model returning to collect bronze colossi

indicators.note: to collect is to gather something inside, so one piece holds the other
returning tells us the model word runs backwards

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to model
a bronze skin tone is a tan

explanation.surface: A model coming back to pick up giant bronze statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so the word stands for anything colossal.

clue.text: One of eight finally finishing early

indicators.note: stopping before the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: Someone among eight runners at last finishes ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight' is a cross-reference to 8-down, TITANS: Atlas was one of the Titans of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas was the Titan condemned to hold up the heavens, one of the Titans at 8-down.

clue.text: Marijuana found on leggings, creating difficult situation

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece found on another follows it

parts.note: tights are leg coverings
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Drugs discovered in someone's leggings land them in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is an idiom for being in an awkward predicament.

clue.text: Spy on me getting changed in Knutsford and Peterlee?

definitions.note: plural examples, marked by the question mark

indicators.note: a changed set of letters has been rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A voyeur spies on someone undressing in two northern English towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Knutsford is said to be named after King Canute (Cnut) and Peterlee, a County Durham new town, after miners' leader Peter Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Each town takes its name from a person, so the place names are eponyms.

clue.text: Greek character to stop running ballet regularly, it's proposed

indicators.note: the Greek letter stops the gap between the pieces, plugging it from within

parts.note: a machine that is on is running

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of ballet

parts.note: theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek actor tries to halt a ballet that keeps being performed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives BLE, the odd letters of the dance word; 'to stop' plugs the Greek letter into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan on the table has been put forward for discussion, an idiom for being proposed.

clue.text: Clown working in safe environment

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown, the Russian-born Coco the Clown
a device that is on is working

explanation.surface: A clown at work in a protected setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown (Nicolai Poliakoff) was a much-loved British circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a silky protective case, and figuratively any sheltered, secure surrounding.

clue.text: Terribly sad result for love cheat

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unfaithful partner meets an awful, unhappy outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An adultress is a married woman who is unfaithful to her husband.

clue.text: Oddball mated with a car seat in barren patch

indicators.note: an oddball is eccentric and out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eccentric coupled with a car seat in a deserted spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddball' looks like a person in the scene but is the anagram signal. The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is a barren tract of land, and the Atacama is a famously arid one.

clue.text: Cable-tie nuts to become chaste

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, signalling the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Fastening oneself with a cable tie to keep out of temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: A celibate person abstains from sex, so is chaste.

clue.text: Material for floor exercise bores coach and gymnast, ultimately

indicators.note: to bore into something is to get inside it

parts.note: a coach is a railway car

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of gymnast

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Floor exercises tire both the coach and the gymnast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor exercise' looks like gymnastics, but the definition ends at 'floor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet is woven textile laid as a covering over floors.

clue.text: Very large game bird

parts.note: OS is short for outsize, the clothing size
game is hunted animals, i.e. prey

explanation.surface: A huge game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.

clue.text: Ring American about old city

parts.note: re means concerning, about
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Phoning an American to talk about an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An areola is a small coloured circle, such as that around a nipple.

clue.text: Left old men evicting Charlie's tenants

indicators.note: evicting throws something out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: codgers are elderly men
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Elderly men left after throwing out a landlord's renters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgers are people who rent a room in someone's house.

clue.text: Get club hit around Spain

indicators.note: the golf shot wraps around the country letter

parts.note: a drive is a long golf shot with a club
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A golfer gets a shot away somewhere around Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to obtain or get it from a source.

clue.text: Animal to give birth in harbour

definitions.meaning: to ... a child is to give birth to it
to ... or harbour a grudge is to hold it

explanation.surface: A creature delivers its young in a port.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a large furry mammal, to give birth, and to hold or harbour a feeling.

clue.text: Improvise parking spot in wood

indicators.note: in puts one piece within the other

parts.note: pear is a timber, the wood of the pear tree
a lay-by is a roadside spot for parking

explanation.surface: Making do with a parking place in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: To play by ear is an idiom for acting without preparation, making it up as you go.

clue.text: Leader of rogue state is party animal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: The head of a rogue nation is a wild partygoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver is someone who goes to all-night dance parties, a hedonistic partygoer.

clue.text: Nearly man Glen

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a valet is a manservant, someone's man

explanation.surface: A man named Glen who is a near miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glen' reads as a man's name but is the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale and a glen are both valleys.

clue.text: Tornados hit hotel, startling hosts

indicators.note: a host holds its guests inside, so the answer is within these words

explanation.surface: Storms batter a hotel, alarming the people running it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tornados were a British instrumental band whose 1962 single Telstar topped the US and UK charts.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1962 single by the Tornados was their big chart-topping record.

clue.text: Piece of meat in bar floozy oddly ignored

parts.note: bar and save both mean except

indicators.note: ignoring the odd letters keeps only the even ones of floozy

explanation.surface: A floozy in a pub is oddly passed over for a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a seasoned red sausage sold in British chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a spicy smoked sausage, a portion of processed meat.
